overview: Session 22 finishes oligopoly with price competition. In standard Bertrand (identical goods, buyers see all prices) undercutting drives price to marginal cost even with two firms; a lower-cost firm prices just under its rival's cost. In differentiated Bertrand, the most common type today, loyal customers let firms price above cost, and price reaction functions slope upward. Bryce's three questions (how many firms compete directly, how much customers overlap, what the main strategic variable is) identify which model fits a market, and the textbook compares all four models on one demand curve.
